prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your location in Houston, whether it’s an emergency, your budget, whether you need repair vs replacement, and any system brand/warranty requirements. That said, here are reliable options and how to pick the best one for your situation.

Well-regarded Houston companies to consider
- John Moore Services — large local company, broad service area, 24/7 emergency service, good local reputation.  
- Baker Brothers Plumbing, Air & Electric — long-standing Houston business, family-owned, strong customer reviews.  
- ARS / Rescue Rooter (Houston) — national company with local technicians, emergency availability and maintenance plans.  
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin franchises — local franchises offering prompt service windows and guarantees.  
- Aire Serv (Houston franchises) — national brand with local presence and maintenance plans.

(These are examples of companies with strong local reputations; I can give more targeted names if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood.)

How to choose the best company for your AC repair
- Verify licensing & insurance: ask for proof of insurance and any required local permits or registration.  
- Technician qualifications: look for NATE-certified techs or manufacturer-authorized repair for your system brand.  
- Read recent reviews: check Google, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB for recent feedback (look for how companies handle follow-up and warranty issues).  
- Get multiple estimates: for anything over a couple hundred dollars, get at least 2–3 written quotes.  
- Ask about warranties and parts: confirm labor and parts warranties and whether they honor manufacturer warranties.  
- Emergency availability & response time: if it’s summer and your system is down, response time matters.  
- Transparent pricing: insist on written estimates and explanations before work begins.

Red flags
- Demanding full payment up front (especially cash-only).  
- Very low bids with high-pressure upsells on arrival.  
- Technicians unwilling to show credentials or provide a written estimate.  
- Numerous unresolved BBB complaints or a pattern of “didn’t fix” reviews.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code, whether this is an emergency, and a few details (central split system or packaged unit, any noises or error codes) and I’ll suggest three highly-rated companies near you and what questions to ask them.
